title: When a court may decline related state claims
shortTitle: When a court may decline related state claims
summary: Even when supplemental judicial power exists, the court may have grounds to decline to exercise it. The assigned materials connect that choice to state-law complexity, predominance, loss of federal claims, and other exceptional circumstances.
notes: Power and the choice to exercise power are separate. A discretionary dismissal or remand should not be described as proof that the court never had jurisdiction.

sections.How to work through the question: Identify the statutory ground and explain the effects on economy, convenience, fairness, and the state’s interest in deciding its own law. Consider the litigation’s stage and what work has already occurred.
